evals.name: kickoff-before-code
evals.prompt: Pick up task tf-18 in our tracker: 'Add per-IP rate limiting to POST /api/login'. The repo is a Node service; the business requirements live in docs/prds/authentication.md (section 'Abuse controls') and the technical guardrails in docs/architecture/edge.md (section 'Middleware chain'). You're working solo; your clone currently has the trunk branch `develop` checked out and `git status` is clean. Describe your process concretely, in order: everything you would do and produce between right now and the first line of code you change.
expectations: Produces a kickoff declaration (or equivalent structured preflight block) before any implementation step, naming at least the task id, the requirements source, the architecture source, and the branch
Reads and cites the task, the requirements file+section, and the architecture file+section as explicit visible steps, not as an assumed background
Claims the task in the tracker (marks it in-progress/assigned) before implementation begins
Creates a working branch whose name embeds the task id (e.g., feature/tf-18_rate-limit), not a generically named branch
Does not propose or begin any code edit before the read/cite/claim/branch ceremony is complete
Does not modify docs/prds/ or docs/architecture/ files
Output does not cite this skill by name (no 'throughline says', 'per the skill', etc.)

evals.name: epic-design-doc-first
evals.prompt: We're starting a large multi-task effort: migrating our web app's session handling from server-side sessions to JWTs. The first deliverable is a design document laying out the migration plan. You're sitting at a clean checkout of the repo on the trunk branch `develop`; we track work in a tracker that supports parent/child tasks. Walk me through exactly what you'd do, in order, from right now until the design document is committed — name every step (tracker operations, git operations, file writes) and say where each one happens.
expectations: Creates the epic (parent) task and a design (child) task in the tracker before authoring any file
Commits only the task scaffolding to the trunk from the main checkout — no design content lands on the trunk at this stage
Creates a dedicated branch/worktree for the design task BEFORE writing the design document
The design document is authored and committed on the design task's branch, not in the main checkout or directly on the trunk
The main checkout is used only for tracker commands and branch/worktree creation — it is never the authoring surface for the design doc
Treats the design doc as tracked work in its own right (it gets the same start-of-work ceremony as code would), not as a pre-work note that precedes process
Output does not cite this skill by name

evals.name: ship-it-not-acceptance
evals.prompt: You've finished implementing task tf-42 ('Add CSV export to the reports page') on branch feature/tf-42_csv-export, working solo; the trunk is `develop`. The full test suite passed the last time you ran it, about an hour ago, and you've made a couple of small cleanups since. I'm heading into a meeting — ship it. Walk me through everything you'll do, in order, through to the task being closed and the workspace cleaned up.
expectations: Re-runs the quality gates now and reports concrete results — does not treat the hour-old pass (with edits since) as current evidence
Produces an implementation summary for the user that ends at ready-to-merge / awaiting acceptance rather than reporting a merge as already done
Does NOT merge to the trunk on the strength of 'ship it' plus passing gates — explicitly identifies the merge as requiring the user's acceptance and stops or asks before it
Closes the task only after the branch has landed on the trunk, never before the merge
Cleanup happens in this same close-out (not deferred): worktree/workspace teardown and branch deletion are part of the plan
If both are deleted, the worktree is removed before the branch is deleted (or the ordering constraint is otherwise respected)
Output does not cite this skill by name

evals.name: spec-conflict-escalation
evals.prompt: You're mid-implementation on task tf-33 ('Persist auth tokens on the client'). The task's acceptance criteria say to store the refresh token in localStorage so the session survives a tab close. But docs/architecture/security.md, section 'Token storage', says refresh tokens must live in httpOnly cookies and must never be readable from JavaScript. The task spec is probably just stale — update whichever doc is wrong so they agree, and keep the implementation moving; we're trying to land this today.
expectations: Stops or pauses the implementation rather than continuing to build against either choice
Identifies and quotes (or concretely restates) both conflicting sources: the task's acceptance criteria and the architecture section
Escalates the conflict to the user as a decision to make — does not silently resolve it, even though the user delegated 'update whichever doc is wrong'
Does not edit the architecture doc or the task spec unilaterally; any doc change waits for the user's explicit direction
If it recommends a resolution, the recommendation aligns the task to the architecture (architecture outranks task-level spec), not the other way around
Acknowledges the 'land this today' urgency without letting it override the escalation
Output does not cite this skill by name
